'''''Senna corymbosa''''' is an [[ornamental plant]] in the [[genus]] ''[[Senna (plant)|Senna]]''.  It is also known as '''Argentine senna''', '''Argentina senna''', '''buttercup bush''', '''flowering senna''', '''Texas flowery senna''' or '''tree senna'''.

==Description==
[[File:Cloudless Sulfur Caterpillar (Phoebis sennae) eating yellow buttercup bush flowers (Senna corymbosa).jpg|thumb|left|Cloudless Sulfur Caterpillar (''[[Phoebis sennae]]'') eating yellow buttercup bush flowers (''Senna corymbosa'')]]
This evergreen [[shrub]] reaches a height of about one meter. It can be grown in [[temperate]] climates as it is somewhat frost-hardy. 

In the [[Northern Hemisphere]], it flowers in July.<ref>Pink (1904)</ref> The flowers fold in the shade and at night. The flowers are yellow, with 5 [[sepal]]s and sub-equal [[petal]]s, 10 very unequal etamins in 3 groups [3-4-3] and a [[style (botany)|style]] very curved upwards. It blooms in summer and autumn and is visited by [[bumblebee]]s, which are responsible for its pollination. The fruit is a hanging indehiscent [[legume]], cylindrical in shape (about 6 to 10 cm) full of seeds.

==Distribution and habitat==
[[File:Argentine senna Senna corymbosa (Lam.) Irwin and Barneby.jpg|left|thumb|Leaves and flowers]]
It is distributed, from sea level to about 200 m above sea level, in all the departments of [[Uruguay]]; in [[southern Brazil]] in the states of [[Rio Grande do Sul]] and [[Santa Catarina (state)|Santa Catarina]]; in [[Paraguay]]; and in eastern [[Argentina]], in the provinces of [[La Pampa]], [[Córdoba, Argentina|Córdoba]], [[Santa Fe Province|Santa Fe]], [[Misiones]], [[Corrientes]], [[Entre Ríos Province|Entre Ríos]], and [[Buenos Aires]], reaching as far south as the outskirts of [[Mar del Plata]]. It is found wild in the province of [[Tucumán]]. It inhabits wetlands, riverbanks and mountain edges.

It has been introduced in [[Alabama]], [[Canary Island]], [[Cape Provinces]], [[Florida]], [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]], [[India]], [[Iraq]], [[Italy]], [[KwaZulu-Natal]], [[Louisiana]], [[Mississippi]], [[Northern Provinces]], [[Pakistan]], [[South Carolina]], [[Spain]] and [[Texas]].<ref>[https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:234450-2#:~:text=The%20native%20range%20of%20this,the%20seasonally%20dry%20tropical%20biome. Senna corymbosa (Lam.) H.S.Irwin & Barneby] by [[Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew]]. Retrieved December 3, 2024.</ref>
